wrong_answers_pool: African populations have the highest mutation rates due to intense solar radiation
African populations interbred with dinosaurs during the Pleistocene
Non-African populations are ancient and have lost all genetic diversity through disease
Africans were the last group to evolve, so they contain all combined traits
Genetic diversity only accumulates in tropical rainforest biomes
It proves that humans evolved simultaneously on all six continents
explanation: Older populations accumulate greater numbers of neutral mutations over time; migrating populations carried only a subset of alleles (founder effect).

question: Pedigree analysis problem 159: A man who has hemophilia (XhY) marries a woman who does not have hemophilia and has no family history of hemophilia (XHXH). What are the chances of their daughters and sons having hemophilia?
correct_answer: 0% of sons have hemophilia, and 100% of daughters are carriers (XHXh)
wrong_answers_pool: 50% of sons have hemophilia, and 50% of daughters are carriers
100% of sons have hemophilia, and 0% of daughters are affected
50% of both sons and daughters have hemophilia
100% of both sons and daughters have hemophilia
25% of sons have hemophilia, and 75% of daughters are affected
All children are completely unaffected and none are carriers
explanation: The father passes Y to all sons (who receive XH from mother, so normal) and Xh to all daughters (who receive XH from mother, making 100% carriers).

question: Chromosome calculation 87: In the species Garden pea (Pisum sativum), the diploid somatic chromosome number is 2n = 14. How many chromosomes will be found in a normal mature gamete after meiosis?
explanation: The gamete is haploid (n): 14 / 2 = 7 chromosomes.

question: Pedigree analysis problem 55: In a family pedigree tracing an inherited genetic condition, two unaffected (normal) parents have a child with the disorder. What does this conclusively indicate about the mode of inheritance?
correct_answer: The condition is caused by a recessive allele, and both parents are heterozygous carriers
wrong_answers_pool: The condition is caused by a dominant allele that mutated spontaneously
The father cannot be the biological parent of the child
The condition is sex-linked dominant inherited exclusively from the father
The condition is caused by non-disjunction of all autosomes
The condition is mitochondrial and inherited from the father
Both parents must be homozygous recessive for the condition
The child must be an identical twin
explanation: If unaffected parents produce an affected offspring, the disorder must be recessive and both parents must carry the hidden recessive allele (e.g. Nn x Nn -> nn).
